Summarize the following fictional project meeting notes in four short English bullet points. Include the main decision, the owners, the deadline, and the unresolved question. Use only the information in the notes. These notes are synthetic test data, not real conversations.

Monday, 09:00. Mira opened the weekly planning meeting for the offline reading application. The team wants to let a reader ask for a short summary of an article without sending the article to a server. The first demonstration should use a small local model and a fixed set of public-domain articles. The team agreed that model quality must be measured separately from whether the application can load a model and display its output.

Monday, 09:10. Arun reported that the basic desktop window can open a text file and show its contents. There is no automatic download feature. A reader chooses an existing model file manually. The window must remain responsive during model loading and generation. Arun will add a visible loading indicator and a cancel button. He will also show a clear error if the chosen file is unreadable or cannot be loaded.

Monday, 09:20. Sofia explained the input budget. The application must count the actual tokens after applying the model's chat template. It must reserve room for the requested answer. If the article is too long, the application should show a clear message instead of silently dropping text. Automatic chunking is a possible later feature, but it is outside the first demonstration. Sofia will prepare short and long synthetic articles for testing this boundary.

Monday, 09:30. Theo proposed comparing two quantized versions of the same model. Mira asked the team to start with one exact file so the first results are reproducible. The model's source revision, file hash, template hash, and quantization will be recorded. Theo will measure loading time and generation speed, but the team will not claim that these measurements apply to other computers. Performance numbers must name the computer and the settings used.

Monday, 09:40. The team discussed cancellation. Pressing cancel should stop work promptly and return the application to a state where another request can run. The application must not replay an interrupted request automatically. Arun will test cancellation during loading and generation. Sofia will check that a cancelled summary is visibly labelled as incomplete and cannot be mistaken for a completed summary.

Monday, 09:50. Mira asked about privacy. The demonstration must work without a network connection once the model has been obtained. Logs may include request identifiers, token counts, timings, and error codes. They must not include the article text or generated summary by default. Theo will check the local diagnostic report to ensure that missing measurements are described as unavailable rather than represented by zero.

Monday, 10:00. The team settled the immediate delivery plan. The demonstration is due on Friday at 16:00. Arun owns the desktop controls and cancellation checks. Sofia owns the fixed text fixtures and the input-budget checks. Theo owns the exact model record and the local performance measurements. Mira will review the demonstration and the evidence before deciding whether to invite additional testers.

Monday, 10:10. One question remains unresolved: should a future mobile version unload the model immediately when the application goes into the background, or first wait for a bounded cancellation period? The team needs an actual device test before choosing the lifecycle policy. This question does not change Friday's desktop-only demonstration. The team also postponed automatic article import, account login, and cloud synchronization.

Monday, 10:15. Mira closed the meeting by repeating the decision: ship a narrow, offline desktop demonstration using one fixed model and fixed test inputs. The demonstration should prove correct loading, bounded input, visible generation, cancellation, and clean repeated use. It is not a release candidate, and it does not establish mobile support or general summarization quality. Each owner will record what passed and what could not be tested.
